native.description: A flat, non-hierarchical classification system organized by behavioral and resource integration patterns rather than substrate or structure. Categories distinguish organisms by their longevity, complexity trajectory, resource sourcing strategy, inter-link connectivity, reproductive output, and gradient positioning.

structural_notation_system.description: Organisms with multi-shift sustained presence (20+ shifts observed), increasing complexity, diverse resource sourcing including inter-links, moderate to high offspring production (1+), and positioning across the gradient. They function as nodes in a resource redistribution network.
characteristic_behaviors: Sustained multi-shift presence with steady complexity growth
Resource integration from cover layer, residue, and inter-links (typically 70%+, 20%+, 1%+ respectively)
Active movement and position adjustment over shifts
One or more offspring (1+ descendants)
Inter-link resource passing (1+ light to others)

structural_isolate.description: Organisms with sustained multi-shift presence and moderate complexity growth, but minimal inter-link participation. Resource sourcing is nearly entirely local (cover layer and residue, <1% inter-link). Single or minimal offspring. Positioned variably on gradient.
characteristic_behaviors: 20+ shift presence with moderate complexity growth
Dominant cover layer sourcing (75%+), secondary residue sourcing
Negligible inter-link activity (<1% of resource intake, <0.5 light passed)
Single offspring or none
Local resource isolation despite gradient position

emergent_incipient.description: Organisms at inception (0 shifts present) with complexity 0, arising from cover layer, positioned mid-range on gradient (0.65–0.75), with moderate architecture. They represent a particular phenotype of nascent entry into the environment.
characteristic_behaviors: Complexity 0, present for 0 shifts, single sighting
No movement, no resource intake, no offspring
Generation 0 (arose from cover layer)
Moderate architectural capacity (reach ~0.70–1.70, 2 link capacity, holding ~7.00 light)
Gradient position mid-range (0.65–0.75)

emergent_ephemeral.description: Organisms at inception (0 shifts present) with complexity 0, arising from cover layer, positioned in lower-gradient range (0.30), with minimal recorded architecture. They represent an alternate nascent phenotype, possibly ephemeral.
characteristic_behaviors: Complexity 0, present for 0 shifts, single sighting

emergent_neonate.description: Organisms at inception (0 shifts present) with complexity 0, positioned near-proximal to data-stream (0.90+), with heavier-built architecture (reach 1.77+, 1–2 link capacity). They may arise from cover layer or descend from generation-1 parents. They represent a nascent phenotype biased toward data-stream proximity with greater architectural capacity.
characteristic_behaviors: Complexity 0, present for 0 shifts, single sighting
No movement, no resource intake, no offspring
Generation 0 or 1 (arose from cover layer or descended from i-00094 or similar)
Gradient position near data-stream (0.90+)
Heavier architectural build (reach 1.77+, 1–2 link capacity, holding 12.50+ light)

emergent_minimal.description: Organisms at inception (0 shifts present) with complexity 0, positioned at or very near the data-stream boundary (0.80–1.00), with minimal ultra-compact architecture (reach ≤1.48, typically 1 link capacity, lowest maintenance costs). They represent an ultra-constrained nascent phenotype at the gradient's extreme.
